result:
The decisive mistake was the Orchestrator's at step 5. The search result at step 4 showed that the Wiktionary entry for "gimlie" says the word comes from Late Latin "camināta". The Orchestrator took that to mean the Spanish word was "caminata". The correct Spanish word shares the spelling of the Latin root, "camināta" without the macron, which is "caminata", so that part was plausible. The task answer ("The World of the Twenty First Century") shows that the Collins entry for the intended word has a 1994 example sentence sourced from that title. The run never reached Collins, because of the Cloudflare block, and it never recovered.

The more decisive failure is the Orchestrator's handling of the block. At step 17 it dropped the Collins path for good and sent the Assistant off to look for alternative sources. The earlier instruction at step 14 had asked WebSurfer only to click through, and the Cloudflare page was never retried (for example, by opening the Bing result URL for the Collins "caminata" page, which appeared at step 28). At step 28 the search result showed the direct Collins page link (collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/spanish-english/caminata). The Orchestrator then never asked WebSurfer to open it, and instead pursued SpanishDict and forum posts, which could not provide Collins's 1994 example sentence.

The error that set the whole path was step 5, where the Orchestrator committed to the chosen word and then directed everything toward it without verifying the Latin root's form. In the task, the Latin root's exact spelling is what links to the Spanish word. The lasting failure from there was never reaching the correct Collins entry.

AGENT: Orchestrator (-> WebSurfer)
STEP: 30
